newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures rise on Australia drought fears.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures rise on Australia drought fears.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose in more active trading on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Wednesday as concern deepened about Australian drought.
A total of 13 lots sold, with near-term May rising 50 cents to A$191.00 a tonne, September 1997 jumping A$5.00 to A$195.00 and January 1998 adding A$1.50 to A$188.00 on the trade.
Settlement prices rose by A$3.00-A$5.00 across the board, with distant September 1998 more than recouping Tuesday's loss.
Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said a squeeze was on the May contract, futures were coming into line with physical prices and wheat was scarce on the east coast.
"The market is concerned about the drought now that it's the end of April and we're going into May," he said.
Increasing numbers of growers were concerned about whether they would put in a crop. Some had decided not to, he said.
A new crop of 17 million tonnes of wheat was more likely than last season's record crop, he said.
Australia produced an estimated 23 million tonnes-plus of wheat in the 1996/97 season ended March 31.
"If the drought continues it could be a lot lower than that ... we could be looking down the barrel of closer to 14.0 million tonnes," he said.
